questions.question: What is the difference between subsistence farming and commercial farming? Give one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Subsistence farming is farming mainly to feed your own family, on a small plot with simple tools and family labour, such as a family growing maize, beans and pumpkins and keeping chickens. Commercial farming is farming mainly to sell for a profit, on large farms with machines and paid workers, such as a maize farm in the Free State or an orange farm in Limpopo.

questions.question: Name the three groups of farm animals with an example of each, and say why sheep are farmed in the Karoo.
questions.expected_answer: Large stock, such as cattle; small stock, such as sheep, goats and pigs; and poultry, such as chickens. Sheep are farmed in the Karoo because it is too dry for crops but has small bushes that sheep can eat, and farmers pump water from boreholes with windmills.

questions.question: Give one example of how transport changed on land, on water and in the air.
questions.expected_answer: On land, people changed from walking and ox-wagons to trains and cars; South Africa's first railway opened in Durban in 1860. On water, people changed from rafts and canoes to sailing ships, steamships and container ships. In the air, people changed from balloons in 1783 to the Wright brothers' aeroplane in 1903 and modern jets.
